summary: Regime read: Tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 68% points tightening, 18% mixed, and 14% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per Bureau of Economic Analysis: Personal Income and Outlays, August 2026). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per Federal Reserve: Governor Waller on the Economic Outlook). Employment is leaning easing and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Lower-Than-Expected Inflation Keeps Fed On Track For October Rate Cut
sources.evidence_text: The piece says September CPI rose more slowly than expected and kept the Fed on track to cut rates in October.
sources.why_it_matters: When inflation undershoots forecasts, the Fed has more room to ease without appearing to risk reaccelerating prices.

sources.title: Tame US inflation gives the Fed room for more rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: ING argued that softer November inflation gave the Fed more room to deliver additional cuts in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A clear disinflation surprise eases the constraint on the Fed's inflation mandate and supports more accommodation.

sources.title: CPI Surprises to the Downside
sources.evidence_text: The article says the latest CPI report came in well below expectations, which improved the odds of Fed rate cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer inflation surprise reduces pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive and supports additional easing.

sources.title: Schedule of Selected Releases 2026
sources.evidence_text: BLS listed upcoming labor-market releases, including JOLTS on September 29 and the Employment Situation on October 2, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Upcoming official data can quickly shift the Fed reaction function if labor conditions weaken more than expected.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index Home, September 2026 Release Schedule
sources.evidence_text: The BLS reported August CPI inflation of 0.4% month over month and scheduled the September CPI release for October 14, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The available inflation reading is not sufficiently current to establish whether easing or tightening pressure is changing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - News & Events
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve's news page lists the September 16, 2026 FOMC press conference as a current event.
sources.why_it_matters: It confirms the timing of the latest policy communication, which frames near-term expectations for cuts or hikes.

sources.title: September Fed Meeting: Updates and Commentary
sources.evidence_text: The article says CME FedWatch and Treasury-market moves pointed to a September 2026 setup in which markets were leaning toward a hike rather than cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: If futures are pricing a hike, the market is signaling the Fed may need to stay tighter than the easing regime would suggest.

sources.title: Fed Rate Probability | FOMC Meeting Odds & Rate Cut Forecast 2026
sources.evidence_text: The page showed a high implied probability of a 25 basis point hike for the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A strong hike probability implies the market expects tighter policy rather than renewed easing.

sources.title: Treasury, 2-Year - Economic Data Series
sources.evidence_text: FRED’s Treasury 2-Year tag shows daily data available through September 14, 2026, confirming the series is current and recently updated.
sources.why_it_matters: Current market data are essential for assessing whether investors are repricing the Fed toward fewer cuts or a higher-for-longer stance.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, citing resilient spending, strong productivity, robust investment, and job gains keeping pace with the workforce.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual rate increase and emphasis on elevated inflation risks indicate that policy has shifted toward tightening rather than remaining in an easing regime.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board and Federal Open Market Committee release economic projections from the September 15-16 FOMC meeting
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve released participants' economic projections associated with the September 15–16 FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: The projections provide the Committee's forward-looking assessment of inflation, employment, growth, and appropriate rates, but the available result does not specify the projected path.

sources.title: September 16, 2026: FOMC Projections
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: FOMC participants projected PCE inflation at 3.7 percent in 2026, 2.3 percent in 2027, 2.1 percent in 2028, and 2.0 percent thereafter.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation remaining materially above target in the near term implies limited scope for additional easing until disinflation becomes more established.

sources.title: US labor market on solid footing; rising mortgages ...
sources.evidence_text: Weekly jobless claims fell to 196,000, the lowest level since mid-July, suggesting labor-market resilience after summer wobble.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger claims data lowers the odds that the Fed will need to ease policy to prevent a labor-market slowdown.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fall
sources.evidence_text: The report also noted that continuing claims fell to 1.730 million, a proxy for hiring that suggests some resilience in labor demand.
sources.why_it_matters: Resilient hiring reduces the odds that the Fed will need to front-load cuts to defend the labor market.

sources.title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference — September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC unanimously raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% and emphasized that inflation remains elevated and above target.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual rate increase and explicit prioritization of price stability indicate that policy is in a tightening phase rather than an easing regime.

sources.title: Producer Price Index up 5.4 percent for the 12 months ended August 2026
sources.evidence_text: Producer prices increased 5.4 percent over the 12 months ended August, with goods up 7.7 percent and services up 4.5 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger pipeline inflation raises the risk that consumer inflation stays sticky, which would keep the Fed cautious.

sources.title: The Fed - Meeting calendars and information
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve calendar schedules the next FOMC meeting for October 27-28, 2026, with the September meeting minutes released on October 7.
sources.why_it_matters: The scheduled meeting and minutes define the next policy decision point but do not themselves indicate whether the reaction function favors easing or tightening.

sources.title: Fed raises rates in search of 'timelier' drop in inflation, sees more hikes
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that the Fed raised rates and signaled more hikes in coming months, with most policymakers anticipating at least one additional quarter-point increase by year-end.
sources.why_it_matters: Forward guidance that points to more hikes directly tightens the reaction function and reduces the odds of imminent cuts.

sources.title: Fed rate decision September 2026: Rates rise to 3.75%-4%
sources.evidence_text: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points and said inflation remained elevated, while its projections showed no increases penciled in after this year and one cut each in 2028 and 2029.
sources.why_it_matters: A fresh hike and elevated inflation language show the Fed is prioritizing price stability over near-term easing.

sources.title: Fed rate tracker — live FOMC cut, hold & hike odds
sources.evidence_text: The tracker says the federal funds target range is 3.75% to 4.00% after the September 15 to 16 FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-implied pricing helps gauge whether investors see the Fed as moving into or staying in a tighter policy setting.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy Calendar
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve scheduled publication of minutes from the September 15–16 FOMC meeting for October 7 and its next policy meeting for October 27–28.
sources.why_it_matters: The calendar provides timing for new reaction-function information but does not itself indicate whether policy is moving toward easing or tightening.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - H.15 - Selected Interest Rates (Daily)
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's daily H.15 release shows the 2-year Treasury yield staying near the upper-4% area in late September.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistently high front-end yields indicate the market is not leaning toward aggressive easing in the near term.

sources.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED
sources.evidence_text: The two-year Treasury yield was 4.83% on October 2, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: An elevated policy-sensitive yield is consistent with markets pricing restrictive policy and fewer imminent cuts.

sources.title: Treasury yields move higher as volatile week wraps up
sources.evidence_text: The story reported the 2-year Treasury yield gained to 4.76% as the week ended.
sources.why_it_matters: A rising 2-year yield after the policy decision suggests markets are leaning toward a tighter expected Fed path.

sources.title: The Fed - September 15-16, 2026 FOMC Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC released its September 15-16, 2026 meeting materials, including the statement and projections, on September 16, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The statement and projections are the clearest official guide to whether the Committee is leaning toward further easing or a tighter stance.

sources.title: VIEW Stocks pull back after Fed raises rates, points to another hike ...
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that the 2-year yield rose after the Fed's latest move, while policy projections showed most officials expected at least one more quarter-point hike by year-end.
sources.why_it_matters: When short rates and Fed dots move higher together, markets and policymakers are both leaning toward fewer cuts or additional tightening.

sources.title: 2-year Treasury yield reaches multi-year high after Fed rate hike
sources.evidence_text: The article says the 2-year Treasury yield hit 4.744% after the Fed hike and that FedWatch-implied odds for another October increase rose to 58%.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising odds of another hike indicate markets are repricing toward tighter policy rather than additional easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve raises federal funds target range to 3.75 ...
sources.evidence_text: The article said the September median policy-rate projection sat above the new target midpoint, consistent with one more quarter-point hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A projected policy rate above the current midpoint implies the Fed is not yet ready to declare an easing cycle.

sources.title: FOMC - September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The summary says the FOMC raised its policy rate by 25 basis points and revised its unemployment and inflation projections upward and downward respectively.
sources.why_it_matters: A rate hike signals the Committee sees inflation persistence as the more important risk than labor-market cooling.

sources.title: The full statement from the Federal Reserve Board for September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The statement says the Committee raised the target range by 25 basis points, noted inflation remains elevated, and said the action supports a timely return to 2 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual hike with explicit inflation concern is the clearest signal that policy is drifting toward tightening rather than easing.

sources.title: Employment and Training Administration
sources.evidence_text: The Labor Department reported 197,000 initial claims for the week ending September 19 and 196,000 for the prior week ending September 12.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistently low claims signal only limited cooling, so the Fed can stay less dovish unless other labor indicators weaken.

sources.title: US Fed Funds Interest Rate: Latest Updates and Trends
sources.evidence_text: The page reports a 73.5% implied probability of another 25 basis point rate increase at the next meeting as of September 24, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing for another hike suggests investors see the Fed reaction function leaning against easing and toward further tightening.

sources.title: September 2026 FOMC rate decision
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4.00%.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual hike is the clearest signal that the Fed judged inflation or labor-market risks to outweigh easing conditions.

sources.title: FOMC Statement: September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC unanimously raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, while most participants projected at least one further increase in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual rate hike combined with broad support for another increase marks a clear shift away from immediate easing.

sources.title: FOMC Meeting Highlights: Fed Signals Another Hike In 2026
sources.evidence_text: The article said CME FedWatch showed more than a 90% probability of a quarter-point hike heading into the meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Heavy pricing of a hike implies markets were already moving away from cuts in response to inflation risk.

sources.title: Implementation Note issued September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve raised the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90% effective September 17, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The implementation details confirm that the higher policy rate was operationally enacted, reinforcing a tightening reaction function.

sources.title: FedWatch
sources.evidence_text: The FedWatch tool showed market-implied probabilities for a higher policy-rate path in late September 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: If markets price a greater chance of hikes, financial conditions tighten and the Fed gets less room to ease.

sources.title: Two-year U.S. Treasury yield reaches new multi-year high
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield touched 4.744%, its highest intraday level since July 2024, alongside CME FedWatch showing a 58% chance of another rate increase in October.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher front-end yield plus hike odds suggests the market expects fewer cuts and potentially more tightening from the Fed.

sources.title: Two-year yield at highest since 2024 after Fed hikes rates
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield hit 4.744% after the Fed’s rate hike, which the article described as the yield’s highest level since July 2024.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is closely tied to expected policy rates, so a move to multi-year highs points to tighter policy expectations.

sources.title: Fed's Interest Rate Decision: September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The summary says the Fed raised rates to 3.75%–4.00% after a stretch of holding steady and described the move as a continuation of a restrictive stance.
sources.why_it_matters: A tighter starting point reduces the odds that the next move is a cut unless inflation and activity soften materially.

sources.title: Release Tables: Unemployment Claims, Weekly
sources.evidence_text: FRED’s weekly claims tables show initial claims at 197,000 and the four-week average at 202,250 for the September 19 release.
sources.why_it_matters: A low and stable claims trend supports the case that the labor market is cooling only modestly, leaving room for cuts rather than hikes.

sources.title: US jobless claims fall to 196,000 during holiday week
sources.evidence_text: Weekly claims declined by 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ended September 12, with the release describing the reading as among the lowest since 1969.
sources.why_it_matters: A resilient claims series argues against near-term tightening in policy support, but it also weakens the case for immediate cuts.

sources.title: September 2026 FOMC Recap
sources.evidence_text: The recap says the September meeting delivered the first Fed hike since 2023 and reflected concern about persistently elevated inflation.
sources.why_it_matters: A first hike after a long pause indicates the Fed is still willing to tighten if inflation risks dominate labor-market softness.

sources.title: CME FedWatch sees 90.4% chance of a September Fed rate hike after August CPI
sources.evidence_text: FedWatch-implied probabilities jumped to about a 90.4% chance of a 25-basis-point hike after the August CPI release.
sources.why_it_matters: When markets price a hike rather than cuts, financial conditions and expectations move in a tighter direction.

sources.title: Latest Numbers : U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
sources.evidence_text: The BLS latest numbers page shows core CPI at 2.4% year over year in August 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Core inflation above 2% suggests underlying price pressures remain inconsistent with a quick return to easier policy.

sources.title: Fed raises US inflation outlook while lowering unemployment forecasts
sources.evidence_text: Reporting on the SEP said the Fed lifted its 2026 core PCE forecast while lowering unemployment projections, implying a stronger inflation focus than labor-market caution.
sources.why_it_matters: If officials see both inflation and employment as firmer, the reaction function shifts away from aggressive easing.

sources.title: Fed hikes in 12-0 vote, commits to inflation fight
sources.evidence_text: The write-up said the Fed lifted 2026 core PCE projections to 3.4% from 3.3% and treated inflation control as the main policy priority.
sources.why_it_matters: A more hawkish inflation stance raises the bar for additional easing if price pressures stay elevated.

sources.title: Fed Outlook 2026: Rate forecasts and fixed income strategies
sources.evidence_text: The piece says markets have shifted from expecting cuts to pricing in the possibility of additional hikes as inflation remains above target.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation stays sticky, the Fed's reaction function shifts toward restraint, making cuts less likely and hikes more plausible.

sources.title: 2026 Speeches
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's speeches index shows a new September 23 speech titled A Long-Term View on the Costs of Shelter.
sources.why_it_matters: A fresh speech on shelter costs may signal continued attention to inflation composition, but the index alone does not reveal policy direction.

sources.title: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, September 2026
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The median projection kept the federal funds rate at 4.1% through 2027 before a modest decline to 3.9% in 2028.
sources.why_it_matters: The delayed and limited projected decline implies that the Fed is not anticipating a rapid return to accommodative policy.

sources.title: Treasury yields are little changed as traders await Fed comments
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield was reported at 4.743% on September 22 while traders waited for Fed commentary.
sources.why_it_matters: A still-elevated front-end yield suggests the market expects policy to remain restrictive, limiting the case for imminent cuts.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury Investors Flock to 2-Year Notes as Yields Near 4.75%, Seen Overpricing Further Fed Tightening
sources.evidence_text: The article says some investors think the 2-year note is already pricing in most of the Fed's further tightening outlook.
sources.why_it_matters: If the front end has already priced in much of the hiking path, the Fed may see less market support for an easing pivot.

sources.title: CME FedWatch: 86% Chance of a 25 bp Fed Rate Hike at ...
sources.evidence_text: The piece reports CME FedWatch odds in the mid-80% range for a 25 bp hike at the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: When futures assign most weight to a hike, the market is pricing a more restrictive policy path than cuts.

sources.title: FOMC September 2026 Odds for a Rate Hike Surpass 50%
sources.evidence_text: The article says traders using CME FedWatch assigned nearly a 56% chance of a quarter-point hike at the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing above 50% for a hike indicates the balance of expected policy outcomes has shifted away from cuts.

sources.title: Fed rate hike Sept 16, 2026: 3.75%-4.00%, One More Coming
sources.evidence_text: The article reports that the Fed raised the target range by 25 bp on September 16, 2026 and that the new projections point to one more quarter-point move by December.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual hike and a projected additional increase both argue for a tightening regime rather than an easing one.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Hits 4.76%, Pricing Out Fed Rate Cuts
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield is reported at 4.76%, its highest reading in the recent range, and the note says the front end is pricing out rate cuts quickly.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher 2-year yield usually signals markets expect a less dovish Fed, which raises the bar for near-term easing.

sources.title: CME FedWatch Prices in 88.7% Chance of 25-Basis-Point ...
sources.evidence_text: Fed funds futures were summarized as giving an 88.7% probability of a 25 bp Fed rate hike at the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Fed funds futures directly encode the market’s expected policy path, so a high hike probability points to tightening expectations.

sources.title: Fed rate decision: markets price 25-bp hike ahead of FOMC, sources say
sources.evidence_text: The piece says markets were pricing roughly a 25 bp hike at the September FOMC meeting and notes the 10-year yield rose above 5% intraday.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising long-end yields alongside hike pricing reinforce a market view that policy will stay tighter for longer.

sources.title: Current Employment Statistics - CES (National)
sources.evidence_text: The BLS national CES page said total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 162,000 in August and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Moderate payroll growth with an unchanged unemployment rate supports a balanced Fed reaction function and does not by itself force tighter policy.

sources.title: US labor market: Defensive stability in a low-hire, low-fire ...
sources.evidence_text: The piece says weekly initial claims have hovered near 200,000 through 2026, indicating a still-subdued layoff environment.
sources.why_it_matters: Subdued layoffs reduce the urgency for Fed tightening and keep the door open to cuts if inflation eases further.

sources.title: Warsh says US economy has strengthened, inflation is the problem
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that Warsh said the economy had strengthened, the labor market was essentially at full employment, and inflation remained the main problem after the rate hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A stronger economy with full employment gives the Fed more room to prioritize inflation control over easing.

sources.title: Fed hikes, hints at more: 7 takeaways from the September FOMC
sources.evidence_text: Market commentary on the meeting emphasized that job gains are keeping pace with workforce growth and that the Fed left the labor-market language largely unchanged.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable labor-market language alongside a hike suggests the Fed does not yet see enough weakening to justify easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The piece said market prices and the median Fed projection pointed to another rate increase in 2026 and additional hikes by mid-2027.
sources.why_it_matters: A market path centered on further hikes implies little room for cuts in the near term.

sources.title: FRED Blog - September 2026
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The blog summarizes the median FOMC projection as 3.4% core PCE inflation in 2026, with a return to the 2% target only by 2029.
sources.why_it_matters: A slower path back to target supports a more restrictive stance than markets may price.

sources.title: Fed review The hike was expected The message was more hawkish
sources.evidence_text: The commentary characterizes the September FOMC message as hawkish, citing resilient spending, stable job growth, and firmer inflation language.
sources.why_it_matters: If the Fed sees demand and labor holding up while inflation stays elevated, it has less reason to cut.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury yields ease as investors await fresh jobs data
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield was reported near 4.74% to 4.77% on 2026-09-22 as traders waited for fresh labor-market data.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term policy pricing can move with incoming jobs data, which the Fed watches closely for signs of labor-market slack or resilience.

sources.title: Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - H.15
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve’s H.15 release showed the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.92% on September 29, 2026, after earlier September readings in the mid-4.6% to mid-4.8% range.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher 2-year yield usually signals markets expect a firmer policy path over the next few quarters, which reduces the room for near-term cuts.

sources.title: Effr
sources.evidence_text: FRED shows the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% on September 22, 2026, with the next release date listed for September 24, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The current policy rate anchors the OIS and futures path, so a stable rate keeps the near-term reaction function focused on incoming data rather than an active easing cycle.

sources.title: US Labor Market Snapshot — September 2026
sources.evidence_text: Indeed said posted wages rose 2.5% over the year ending August 2026 and described the labor market as broadly stable with low layoffs.
sources.why_it_matters: Slower wage growth and stable layoffs ease pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims decrease as labor market regains footing
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims slipped to 197,000 in the week ended September 19, while continuing claims rose slightly to 1.719 million.
sources.why_it_matters: Low initial claims argue against a rapidly cooling labor market, though a small rise in continuing claims keeps recession risk on the radar.

sources.title: Summary of Economic Projections, September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: FOMC participants projected PCE inflation at 3.7% in 2026, declining to 2.3% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028.
sources.why_it_matters: The elevated near-term inflation path implies that rapid rate cuts would be inconsistent with the Committee’s baseline reaction function.

sources.title: The New York Fed DSGE Model Forecast—September 2026
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The New York Fed’s September model forecast still expects core PCE inflation to decline toward target only gradually over the next several years.
sources.why_it_matters: A slow glide path to 2% supports patience on easing and argues against an aggressive cutting cycle.

sources.title: Why Hike | Tom Barkin | Inflation | Employment
sources.evidence_text: Barkin said inflation risks outweighed maximum-employment risks and noted that the labor market continued to look healthy.
sources.why_it_matters: When a policymaker judges inflation risk as dominant, the bar for additional easing rises materially.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - 2026 Speeches
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's speeches index shows additional remarks published during the week of September 23, 2026, including Governor Barr's shelter-focused speech.
sources.why_it_matters: This is a pointer to fresh Fed communications that can shift market expectations, but it does not itself signal easing or tightening.

sources.title: Federal Reserve recent postings
sources.evidence_text: The Fed posted the September 15-16 FOMC economic projections shortly after the meeting, reinforcing that the latest policy update is the main guide for the next decision.
sources.why_it_matters: The latest projection set is the clearest read on the Fed's reaction function until fresh labor and inflation data arrive.

sources.title: Wall St Week Ahead Jobs report, inflation data to test US rate path economic
sources.evidence_text: A Reuters poll of economists expected the September payroll report to show 100,000 job gains and unemployment at 4.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: Market expectations for a softer but still positive labor market suggest only limited immediate pressure on the Fed either to ease aggressively or tighten further.

sources.title: News Releases
sources.evidence_text: Initial jobless claims fell to 197,000 for the week ending September 19, with the prior week revised up to 198,000.
sources.why_it_matters: Low claims argue against rapid labor-market deterioration, which reduces urgency for aggressive Fed easing.

sources.title: US Weekly Jobless Claims Near 57-Year Lows as Labor Market Regains Footing
sources.evidence_text: The article framed the latest claims report as evidence that jobless claims remain near multi-decade lows and layoffs are limited.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent low claims imply limited labor-market slack, which supports patience on rate cuts but not a need for hikes.

sources.title: US Jobless Claims Slip to 197000, Remain Historically Low
sources.evidence_text: Bloomberg described claims at 197,000 as historically low and close to multi-decade lows.
sources.why_it_matters: A still-firm labor market makes it harder for the Fed to justify imminent cuts on employment weakness.

sources.title: US Jobless Claims Fall Toward 6-Decade Low
sources.evidence_text: The report said continuing claims rose only slightly to 1.719 million while remaining near multi-year lows.
sources.why_it_matters: Modest continuing claims can indicate only gradual cooling, which supports patience rather than an immediate tightening bias.

sources.title: Fed again hoping for a pain-free landing from current inflation spike
sources.evidence_text: The piece said the Fed was focused on keeping the labor market near full employment while still prioritizing inflation control after the September hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A policy mix that tolerates a strong labor market while maintaining restrictive bias is consistent with fewer cuts, not an easing pivot.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - Calendar: September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Fed calendar shows a dense run of public appearances by policymakers throughout late September 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A crowded Fed speaking schedule can move market expectations as officials reinforce or soften the post-meeting policy bias.

sources.title: Text of Fed's September Monetary-Policy Statement
sources.evidence_text: The statement said job gains kept pace with the workforce, unemployment had changed little, inflation remained elevated, and policy action would support a timelier return to the 2 percent goal.
sources.why_it_matters: The Fed described labor conditions as stable while emphasizing elevated inflation, which supports tighter policy rather than easing.

sources.title: Interest Rates Products
sources.evidence_text: CME’s interest-rate market page links FOMC move probabilities, target ranges, and historical rate data in one place.
sources.why_it_matters: It is the market reference point for whether futures are implying fewer cuts or even hikes.

sources.title: Oil jump sends 30-year yields to two-decade high
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that 2-year Treasury yields rose and Fed funds futures were pricing a majority probability of a Fed hike next month.
sources.why_it_matters: That combination implies the market is drifting toward tighter policy expectations rather than more easing.

sources.title: 2-year Treasury note yield highest since May 2024 as traders increased hike bets
sources.evidence_text: The article says the 2-year Treasury yield jumped more than 11 basis points to 4.889% and that traders increased bets the Fed would need to hike again in October.
sources.why_it_matters: If traders are shifting toward another hike, the market is signaling the Fed may need to stay tighter for longer.

sources.title: US Treasury yields edge up as rate hike bets weigh on markets
sources.evidence_text: The piece reports the 2-year Treasury yield reached 4.7879% and that CME FedWatch showed a 53% probability of another Fed rate increase at the October meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Pricing of a near-term hike directly points to tighter expected Fed policy rather than continued easing.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury yield hits 4.85% after a 14 basis point surge
sources.evidence_text: The article describes a 14 basis point jump in the 2-year yield to 4.85% and frames it as the market pricing tighter policy.
sources.why_it_matters: The front end of the curve is one of the clearest real-time gauges of how restrictive the Fed is expected to be.

sources.title: 2026 TED Archive : The Economics Daily
sources.evidence_text: BLS said payroll employment rose 162,000 in August 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A solid but not overheating payroll gain argues against immediate tightening while still leaving the Fed room to keep policy restrictive if inflation stays sticky.

sources.title: US Jobs Report Seen Showing 90,000 Payrolls, 4.1% Unemployment Rate
sources.evidence_text: Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected September payroll growth to slow to about 90,000 while unemployment stayed at 4.1 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer expected payroll print would support the view that labor demand is cooling enough to justify easier policy if inflation cooperates.

sources.title: News Release
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims for the week ending September 19 were 197,000, down 1,000 from the prior week.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower claims reinforce the view that layoffs remain contained, which reduces urgency for the Fed to tighten policy.

sources.title: Initial Claims (ICSA)
sources.publisher: FRED / Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: FRED’s time series shows seasonally adjusted initial claims at 197,000 for the week ending September 19, with prior weeks near 198,000 and 207,000.
sources.why_it_matters: The claims trend is still historically low, so by itself it does not force the Fed toward easier policy, but it also does not justify tighter policy beyond the existing hike.

sources.title: Inflation Nowcasting
sources.evidence_text: The Cleveland Fed nowcast showed September 2026 CPI at 3.57 percent and PCE at 3.97 percent, with core PCE at 3.49 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: If realized inflation tracks this nowcast, the Fed would face stronger pressure to delay further easing.

sources.title: SEPTEMBER 24 2026 Opening Remarks
sources.evidence_text: Paulson said underlying inflation is still running about 2.5 to 3 percent, that price stability needs attention, and that she supported the rate increase at the prior week's meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent inflation above target supports a tighter stance because it argues against rapid easing even if employment remains solid.

sources.title: Fed's Barr sees further policy moves as U.S. inflation ...
sources.publisher: SANA (reporting Barr remarks at Chicago Fed event)
sources.evidence_text: Barr said further policy adjustments are likely needed to return inflation to 2 percent in a timely manner, while noting the labor market remains solid.
sources.why_it_matters: If policymakers expect more adjustments, the reaction function is leaning against easing until inflation convincingly converges to target.

sources.title: The Fed - Live Video - Federal Reserve
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve scheduled and streamed the September 16, 2026 FOMC press conference live.
sources.why_it_matters: The press conference is where the Fed often clarifies whether a policy move is a one-off or the start of a broader tightening bias.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Rates — September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury reported a 2-year par yield of 3.98% on September 18, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A 2-year yield near 4% is consistent with markets pricing a relatively restrictive policy path after the FOMC hike.

sources.title: What's The Fed's Next Move?
sources.evidence_text: This research note says the September meeting delivered a 25 bp hike, implying the market and policy path are now shifted away from cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A research view that the next leg of policy is higher rather than lower reinforces a tighter expected path in the near term.

sources.title: Treasury Yield Curve Bounces From 2026's Flattest Point
sources.evidence_text: The piece says the 2-year Treasury yield tracked the part of the curve that reflects Fed policy expectations most closely and closed the week at 4.81%.
sources.why_it_matters: When the policy-sensitive front end rises, it usually signals the market expects a less accommodative Fed path.

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims — Week Ending September 19, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Initial unemployment claims were 197,000 for the week ending September 19, and the four-week average fell to 202,250.
sources.why_it_matters: Claims remain historically low and are not signaling a material labor-market break that would compel faster easing.

sources.title: Fed raises rates in search of timelier drop in inflation, sees more hikes
sources.evidence_text: The Fed raised rates on September 16 and signaled additional hikes in coming months while projecting a higher policy rate path.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual rate hike and a higher projected path directly shift the reaction function toward tighter policy and away from near-term cuts.

sources.title: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Summary
sources.evidence_text: The BLS said the September 2026 JOLTS release was scheduled for November 3, so no newer openings data were yet available in this period.
sources.why_it_matters: Absent fresh openings data, the Fed is likely to lean on existing evidence of labor tightness rather than assume slack is building.

sources.title: Schedule of Releases for the Employment Situation
sources.evidence_text: The BLS schedule showed the September Employment Situation release was due on October 2, confirming that the labor-market data window was still incomplete.
sources.why_it_matters: The Fed cannot update its labor assessment with the main payroll report until the scheduled release, limiting any immediate policy reaction.

sources.title: FOMC Statement: September 2026 | J.P. Morgan Asset Management
sources.evidence_text: The September SEP showed a higher 2026 core PCE forecast and a median policy path that ended 2026 above the prior level.
sources.why_it_matters: If the Fed’s own projections point to higher inflation and a higher terminal rate, that reduces the odds of near-term cuts.

sources.title: 2026 FOMC Press Releases
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's press release archive shows both the FOMC statement and the September economic projections were released on September 16, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The projections help reveal whether policymakers see the next move as more likely to be further restraint than renewed easing.

sources.title: Schedule of Releases for the Consumer Price Index
sources.evidence_text: The CPI release schedule shows September 2026 CPI is set for October 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM Eastern.
sources.why_it_matters: The timing matters because the next inflation report can quickly change expectations for cuts versus holds.

sources.title: Fed's Williams: 'Reasonable' to expect another rate hike by year-end
sources.evidence_text: CNBC reported that Williams said it was reasonable to expect another rate hike by year-end.
sources.why_it_matters: A senior Fed official endorsing another hike points to an active tightening bias rather than a pivot to cuts.

sources.title: Major brokerages see one more Fed rate hike in 2026 after strong signals
sources.evidence_text: Reuters said rate futures were pricing about a 90% probability of another quarter-point Fed hike by year-end after the latest Fed signal.
sources.why_it_matters: When futures lean toward another hike, the 2-year yield tends to stay elevated because the market expects a tighter policy path.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Dips to 4.71%, Signaling a Shift in Fed Rate Bets
sources.evidence_text: The article said the 2-year Treasury yield fell to 4.71% on September 23 and interpreted the move as pricing a more accommodative Fed path.
sources.why_it_matters: A lower 2-year yield would usually support the case for more easing by indicating softer expected short-rate settings ahead.

sources.title: Fed meeting live updates: Fed hikes interest rates by 25 basis points for ...
sources.evidence_text: Coverage of the September FOMC meeting said the Committee moved to a higher policy-rate setting and emphasized persistent inflation alongside resilient jobs.
sources.why_it_matters: A policy move framed around persistent inflation and solid labor conditions signals a reaction function that is less willing to ease quickly.

sources.title: Labor market is more stable than a year ago, new data shows
sources.evidence_text: The report said continued and new claims both improved, reinforcing the view that the labor market is sturdier than a year ago.
sources.why_it_matters: A sturdier labor market gives the Fed more room to prioritize inflation control rather than preemptive cuts.

sources.title: Personal Income and Outlays, August 2026
sources.evidence_text: The headline PCE price index rose 3.4% over the year through August 2026, remaining materially above the Federal Reserve’s 2% objective.
sources.why_it_matters: Above-target PCE inflation limits the scope for near-term easing and reinforces restrictive policy.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index
sources.evidence_text: The August 2026 PCE price index increased 3.4% from a year earlier, unchanged from July.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent inflation well above the Fed’s 2% target supports maintaining or increasing restriction rather than accelerating cuts.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index Excluding Food and Energy
sources.evidence_text: Core PCE inflation was 3.0 percent in August from a year earlier, unchanged from July.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent core inflation above target argues for patience and makes further cuts more conditional on disinflation.

sources.title: Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate
sources.evidence_text: The Dallas Fed’s trimmed-mean PCE page updated on September 30 and states that overall PCE inflation was 3.4 percent and core PCE inflation was 3.0 percent on a 12-month basis.
sources.why_it_matters: Trimmed-mean inflation is a useful underlying-trend signal, and readings well above target argue for keeping policy restrictive.

sources.title: Market sees next Fed hike in October, following Barr comments hot inflation
sources.evidence_text: CNBC reported that CME FedWatch showed a 73% probability of a rate hike at the October 27-28 FOMC meeting after hotter inflation and Barr remarks.
sources.why_it_matters: A shift toward a hike probability signals that inflation data are overpowering any easing impulse in the Fed reaction function.

sources.title: Current U.S. Inflation Rates: 2000-2026
sources.evidence_text: The page states that U.S. annual inflation was 3.4% for the 12 months ending August 2026, matching July's rate after the September 11 BLS release.
sources.why_it_matters: Sticky inflation above target makes it harder for the Fed to justify cutting without seeing clearer disinflation.

sources.title: 2-Year T-Note Futures Quotes
sources.evidence_text: CME’s 2-year Treasury note futures page highlights the front-end rate sensitivity of the contract, aligning it with shifting expectations for the Fed path.
sources.why_it_matters: Movements in 2-year Treasury pricing are a key market-based read on whether the Fed is expected to ease or stay restrictive.

sources.title: Stocks Tumble as Yields Surge
sources.evidence_text: The piece says October hike odds jumped sharply and that more hikes were being priced through 2027, which implies the market was moving away from cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A repricing toward additional hikes suggests financial markets expect the Fed to remain restrictive for longer.

sources.title: Fed's Williams sees no urgency for next rate hike
sources.evidence_text: Williams said there was no need for urgency after the September policy move.
sources.why_it_matters: That tone tempers the near-term tightening impulse and leaves room for incoming data to slow further hikes.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Jumps to 4.92%, Signaling More Fed Tightening
sources.evidence_text: The article said the 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.92% on September 29 and framed the move as the market pricing more Fed tightening.
sources.why_it_matters: This kind of repricing matters because the Fed watches financial conditions and market expectations when assessing whether policy is still restrictive enough.

sources.title: Employment Situation Summary - 2026 M09 Results
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payroll employment increased by 29,000 in September, the unemployment rate was 4.2 percent, and average hourly earnings rose 0.1 percent month over month and 3.0 percent year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: Weak job creation alongside contained wage growth reduces labor-market overheating risk and supports additional policy easing.

sources.title: Jobs report September 2026
sources.evidence_text: September payroll growth substantially undershot expectations, while annual wage growth slowed to 3.0 percent, its weakest pace since May 2021.
sources.why_it_matters: A downside employment surprise with cooling wages supports patience or future cuts rather than additional tightening.

sources.title: Employment Situation News Release - September 2026 Results
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payroll employment increased by 29,000 in September, the unemployment rate was 4.2 percent, and average hourly earnings rose 0.1 percent month over month.
sources.why_it_matters: Weak hiring and subdued wage growth reduce labor-market pressure on inflation and support a less restrictive Federal Reserve stance.

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims — Week Ending September 12, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Initial unemployment claims fell to 196,000 for the week ending September 12, while the four-week average declined to 203,250 and insured unemployment also decreased.
sources.why_it_matters: Firm claims and declining continuing unemployment indicate limited labor-market deterioration, reducing near-term pressure for additional Fed cuts.

sources.title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: Jefferson said labor-market conditions had stabilized, unemployment was near maximum employment, and he supported the September rate increase to 3.75%–4.00%.
sources.why_it_matters: A stabilized labor market near maximum employment gives policymakers room to prioritize inflation control over rate cuts.

sources.title: Employment Situation — September 2026
sources.evidence_text: September payroll employment increased by 29,000, while the unemployment rate held at 4.2 percent and employment in major industries changed little.
sources.why_it_matters: Very weak hiring with stable unemployment indicates softer labor-market momentum, increasing the case for additional rate cuts if inflation continues to moderate.

sources.title: Economic Conditions and Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: Barr said inflation remained significantly above target while consumer spending and business investment supported a solid labor market, and noted that the FOMC had raised rates earlier in the month.
sources.why_it_matters: A policymaker’s assessment that inflation risks have increased while labor-market risks have receded supports fewer cuts and a tighter reaction-function stance.

sources.title: State Employment and Unemployment Summary
sources.evidence_text: The BLS released its state employment and unemployment summary on September 18, 2026, while national labor-market conditions remained broadly stable.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable employment conditions do not provide a strong additional signal for either faster easing or further tightening.

sources.title: Fed Raises Rates in September, Officials Signal One More Hike in 2026
sources.evidence_text: The September dot plot was described as more hawkish than in June, with officials signaling that policy would remain restrictive until inflation showed more convincing progress toward 2%.
sources.why_it_matters: The inflation threshold for future easing appears higher, reducing the likelihood of near-term cuts.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Pulls Back to 4.81% After a Long Climb
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield reportedly fell 6 basis points to 4.81% after approaching 5%.
sources.why_it_matters: A decline in the policy-sensitive 2-year yield can signal reduced expectations for additional tightening, although the level remains elevated.

sources.title: CPI Home
sources.evidence_text: BLS had scheduled the September CPI release for October 14, so no September CPI reading was available in the source update.
sources.why_it_matters: The absence of a new CPI reading leaves the Fed reliant on existing evidence of above-target inflation rather than a fresh easing signal.

sources.title: Treasury yields fall after weak September jobs report
sources.evidence_text: Following a weaker September jobs report, the 2-year Treasury yield fell six basis points to 4.73%, while CME FedWatch showed an 84% probability of no October rate change.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower front-end yields and reduced immediate hike pricing indicate markets see weaker employment as limiting further tightening, although they do not establish a return to cuts.

sources.title: Fed rate hike odds decline after September jobs report
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing showed the probability of an October quarter-point hike near 17%, down from about 36% a week earlier after a weaker-than-expected September employment report.
sources.why_it_matters: Reduced near-term hike pricing suggests labor-market weakness is tempering the Fed’s tightening bias.

sources.title: Williams Says the Fed Has Time. October Rate Hike Odds Fell Below a Coin Flip
sources.evidence_text: New York Fed President John Williams indicated that policymakers had time to gather information and did not need to act urgently, while December tightening remained possible.
sources.why_it_matters: An emphasis on patience lowers the likelihood of immediate tightening without removing the option of a later hike.

sources.title: Fed Still on Track to Hike Interest Rates in October?
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch hike pricing reportedly fell from 64% to 28%, while policymakers still left open the possibility of one additional increase later in the year.
sources.why_it_matters: The immediate tightening impulse weakened, but persistent later-year hike risk means policy has not clearly returned to an easing regime.

sources.title: Fed Raises Rates for First Time Since 2023 as Inflation Outlook Worsens
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Open Market Committee reportedly raised the target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% on September 16 and projected a further increase in its median year-end rate outlook.
sources.why_it_matters: An enacted rate increase and higher projected policy path are strong evidence that the prevailing regime is tightening rather than easing.

sources.title: Employment report September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The report showed slower payroll growth, a modest rise in unemployment, and wage growth easing to 3.0 percent year over year, strengthening the case for Federal Reserve patience.
sources.why_it_matters: The combined labor-market signals lower the urgency for further rate increases, although they do not by themselves require an immediate cut.

sources.title: Weekly Unemployment Insurance Claims, Week Ending September 26, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims fell to 197,000 for the week ending September 26, while the four-week moving average declined to 200,000.
sources.why_it_matters: Low and falling claims indicate limited labor-market stress, reducing the case for easing.

sources.title: Fed: October Rate-Hike Odds Slide Below 22% Ahead of Minutes
sources.evidence_text: CME-derived pricing put the probability of at least a 25-basis-point October hike near 22%, down from roughly 51% a week earlier, while December pricing still favored a higher policy rate.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term easing in rate expectations argues against an imminent hike, but the forward curve still embeds tightening risk beyond the next meeting.

sources.title: FOMC Minutes, September 15–16, 2026 Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC unanimously raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, citing elevated inflation and a labor market near full employment.
sources.why_it_matters: An enacted rate hike and concern about elevated inflation indicate the reaction function had shifted toward tighter policy.

sources.title: Governor Waller on the Economic Outlook
sources.evidence_text: Waller characterized the labor market as stable, inflation as too high, and reported that most September meeting participants expected at least one more rate increase this year.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable employment alongside excessive inflation supports further tightening rather than near-term cuts.

sources.title: September 2026 Employment Situation
sources.evidence_text: September payroll employment increased by 29,000 and the unemployment rate was 4.2%, with little change across major industries.
sources.why_it_matters: Weak payroll growth argues against aggressive tightening, but the low unemployment rate does not create a strong case for cuts by itself.

sources.title: Economic News Releases - State Employment and Unemployment
sources.evidence_text: The BLS issued its monthly state employment and unemployment release for August 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: State-level labor data inform the employment side of the dual mandate, but the available release summary does not establish a clear national direction for policy.

sources.title: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey News Release
sources.evidence_text: The BLS JOLTS release page was updated on September 29, 2026, but the available summary does not provide the underlying August labor-market figures.
sources.why_it_matters: Without the reported openings, hires, and separations data, the release cannot be scored reliably for easing or tightening pressure.

sources.title: U.S. Economy at a Glance
sources.evidence_text: The August release reported that personal consumption expenditures rose 0.9% month over month, while personal income increased 0.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: Strong consumption can sustain demand-driven price pressure, but the cited release summary does not provide the PCE inflation rate needed for a stronger reaction-function signal.

sources.title: BLS Weekly Update
sources.evidence_text: BLS reported that nonfuel import prices rose 5.5 percent over the year through August 2026, the largest annual increase since May 2022.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher import-price growth can add to inflation persistence and make policymakers less willing to accelerate rate cuts.

sources.title: Employment Situation Summary
sources.evidence_text: The BLS summary lists a 4.2% unemployment rate and a preliminary payroll increase of 29,000 for September 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable unemployment alongside weak payroll growth creates conflicting signals, limiting a clear labor-market case for either cuts or hikes.

sources.title: Fed minutes reveal another hike likely before year end amid elevated inflation
sources.evidence_text: Reported CME FedWatch pricing put the probability of an October hike at 17.2% and a December hike to 4.00%–4.25% at 70.5%, with a 13.9% probability of a further December hike to 4.25%–4.50%.
sources.why_it_matters: The concentration of hike risk in December indicates markets have shifted from expecting easing toward anticipating additional restraint later in the year.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Dips to 4.79% as Fed Signals More
sources.evidence_text: The two-year Treasury yield settled at 4.79% on October 6 after falling five basis points from recent highs despite expectations for another hike.
sources.why_it_matters: The pullback offsets some tightening signal from the elevated level but does not establish a durable return to an easing regime.

sources.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, September 15–16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The minutes state that all participants supported raising the policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%.
sources.why_it_matters: Unanimous support indicates broad Committee agreement that tighter policy was appropriate in response to the economic outlook.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates, September 30, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury curve data show a 2-year par yield of 4.02% on September 30, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is closely linked to expected near-term policy and, at this level after a rate hike, is consistent with reduced expectations for immediate easing.
